description: Colombia's drinking water quality surveillance system SIVICAP produces the IRCA (Índice de Riesgo de la Calidad del Agua para Consumo Humano), the percentage risk of water-related disease from failures to meet physical, chemical and microbiological standards. The national dataset gives the annual average IRCA and its risk level for every department and municipality, separately for urban and rural areas, from 2007; on 2026-09-26 it held 19,160 rows covering 2007 to 2024. The Instituto Nacional de Salud produced it and publishes it on the national open data portal. Coverage is national for Colombia. It is free on datos.gov.co as CSV or JSON through the Socrata API under CC BY-SA 4.0, updated yearly (last on 2025-06-10), and iMMAP republished 2010 to 2019 values with the consolidated SIVICAP parameters on HDX. Caveats: it is an index of sampled water quality, not a description of the supply systems, and the latest year when read was 2024. Simulation uses: municipal drinking water quality risk as an indicator of service performance and health exposure, and to flag systems for improvement. Related records: the WHO/UNICEF JMP database (data-who-unicef-jmp-wash-database) and SIASAR (data-siasar-rural-water-sanitation-information-system).
